title: POC Weekly Security Sync - ZenithHealth
summary: Weekly POC security check-in: reviewed SSO/SAML test status, audit log availability and format, data retention/retention policy for pilot, SOC 2 evidentiary requests, KMS/encryption questions, and next steps for delivering security artifacts and scheduling a deeper compliance review. Agreed to a short security deep-dive next week and deliver sample audit logs and SOC2 attestation. Some minor transcription noise and speaker overlap in parts.

Data retention and purging during pilot
SOC 2 and compliance artifacts for pilot
Next steps: docs and demo setup

SE to provide sample audit log export (Daniel) by 2025-05-12
ZenithHealth to provide SSO metadata and test user list (Maya) by 2025-05-08
Schedule security deep-dive (1 hour) w/ Zenith security & Redwood SEs for week of 2025-05-12 (Ava)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava M (Redwood AE), Daniel C (Redwood SE), Priya P (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Zenith Sec), Maya Singh (Zenith Cloud), Carlos Rivera (Zenith Privacy), Tara Bloom (Product)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call -- we doing okay on audio?
[00:05] Liam: Yep, all good.
[00:08] Daniel: mic's good.
[00:10] Ava: Great. This is the weekly POC security sync. Main goals today: SSO tests, audit logs and retention, SOC2 requests, and any open blockers for the pilot. Priya's taking notes for next steps.
[00:25] Maya: Quick status — we ran the SAML test yesterday, we hit a couple of issues where the assertion issuer didn't match what our IdP expected, and there were some clock skew warnings. I'll share the IdP logs after.
[00:36] Daniel: okay that aligns with what we saw on the redwood side, the metadata had a slightly different entityID. We pushed a config variant to the test tenant, can you try swapping the entityID and re-run? Also we have a test user set: zenith-test1@zenithhealth.com.
[00:50] Maya: yep will do.
[00:53] Liam: From a compliance angle, we want to confirm SSO binds are using Encrypted assertions and that session timeouts map to our SSO session policy.
[01:05] Ava: Redwood supports signed and encrypted assertions; session timeout mapping is configurable at the tenant level, we can demo the settings. Daniel, can you surface that in the security deep-dive?
[01:15] Daniel: yes, I'll prepare a short demo — also show RBAC mapping from IdP groups to Redwood roles.
[01:23] Tara: quick Q: if we move to dedicated later, will the SSO config differ?
[01:28] Daniel: For Dedicated/Private, it's the same SAML metadata flow but you'll point to your VPC endpoint and we support customer-controlled certs/KMS. There are some network-level configs for on-prem that we'll document.
[01:40] Carlos: Audit logs — what schema do they have and can they be exported to our SIEM? We use Splunk.
[01:48] Daniel: Audit logs include event_time, user_id, action, route, model_id, token_count, request_id, and a truncated prompt hash for privacy. We can stream logs to S3 or push via Kinesis/HTTP to your collector. We have a sample JSON export.
[02:05] Ava: we'll send the sample log file after the call — Daniel, attach the sample and a field mapping doc.
[02:12] Daniel: noted.
[02:15] Liam: Retention — during pilot we need logs retained for 90 days and have the ability to request a one-off export before purge. How does Redwood handle purge?
[02:25] Daniel: retention is configurable per-tenant; default hosted retention is 30 days, but we can set pilot tenants to 90 days. Purge runs daily; we can perform manual snapshot exports prior to purge on request. For Private, you control retention fully.
[02:40] Carlos: Need to confirm encryption at rest details — server-side encryption vs customer-managed keys.
[02:46] Daniel: Hosted default is server-side encryption with provider-managed keys; we support KMS integration for customer-managed keys for Dedicated or Private as an add-on. We can share our KMS integration doc.
[02:58] Tara: SOC 2 — we opened a request with procurement; what evidence can you provide for the pilot?
[03:05] Ava: we can provide SOC2 Type II report, a controls matrix mapping to common frameworks, and a pen test summary. For pilot, we can also give a scoped set of logs and control artifacts.
[03:15] Liam: we'll need the Type II and the mapping by early next week to satisfy internal procurement gating.
[03:22] Ava: understood, we'll get that by Friday.
[03:25] Maya: small nit — during the load tests we saw a few 503s, is there any risk those are access-related rather than capacity?
[03:32] Daniel: the 503s were traced to temporary capacity scaling on the shared tier; for pilot tenants on hosted we can provision burst capacity or move to a reserved Dedicated pool to avoid that. We also have circuit-breaker logs to show why a request was rerouted.
[03:45] Carlos: Can you provide those circuit-breaker logs for our review?
[03:49] Daniel: yes, we'll include a short extract with request_ids and timestamps (redacted where needed).
[03:55] Priya: I'm capturing all of these as action items and will follow up in the CRM.
[04:00] Ava: Great. Next — data residency: Zenith's policy requires EU data residency for EU patients. Our pilot traffic includes EU data; how is data segmented?
[04:12] Daniel: Redwood routes by region; the hosted control plane can pin model inferencing to eu-west-1 for EU traffic. We also support VPC endpoints and private deployments for strict residency. For the pilot we can set the tenant region and validate logs show eu-west endpoints.
[04:30] Liam: Good. Also want to confirm audit log redaction — prompt content should be truncated or hashed.
[04:37] Daniel: prompts are hashed/truncated depending on config; full prompt content is not stored by default for hosted pilot unless you opt-in. We'll include the exact configuration options in the sample log doc.
[04:50] Tara: On data deletion, if we request a purge for a user, is there a user-level purge or only tenant-level?
[04:58] Daniel: we support both: individual request-level purge (best-effort) and tenant-level purge. There is an API to submit a deletion request and we can produce audit trail events for that.
[05:08] Carlos: For compliance we need to see the deletion audit trail included in logs.
[05:12] Daniel: yes, deletion events are surfaced in the audit log with event_type = deletion_request and status.
[05:18] Liam: Any unresolved blockers?
[05:21] Maya: SSO fix — I will re-run after I get the updated entityID; if that still fails, I'll share the IdP logs.
[05:27] Daniel: we'll standby.
[05:30] Ava: SOC2 artifacts by Friday. Daniel will send sample logs by Monday. Maya will provide SSO metadata by tomorrow. Scheduling a 60-min security deep-dive next week.
[05:41] Tara: Quick procurement Q: will the pilot generate billable usage? We're on a trial credit but need to know how overages are handled.
[05:50] Ava: for the pilot we can cap usage; we'll coordinate with billing and let you know the overage policy.
[05:57] Carlos: encryption questions — can you provide network diagram with where keys live?
[06:02] Daniel: yes, we'll attach a high-level network/arch diagram and KMS flow chart.
[06:10] Priya: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and attach the docs once we have them.
[06:15] Ava: ok let's recap next steps.
[06:18] Daniel: Send sample audit logs + field map (Daniel)
[06:20] Ava: Send SOC2 + pen test + controls mapping (Ava)
[06:22] Maya: Provide SSO metadata and test users (Maya)
[06:24] Carlos: Confirm retention policy and any special legal hold needs (Carlos)
[06:28] Ava: I'll set the security deep-dive for next week and invite the relevant engineers.
[06:32] Liam: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:35] Ava: Thanks, we'll follow up in the CRM and send the artifacts.
[06:39] Meeting end.

Notes on quality: occasional mis-attribution where redwood names are shortened; some ASR errors in product names in other calls, but this file is fairly legible.
